title: Functoriality of the sequential derived inverse limit
statement:
Let $\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T)$ be the tower category of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], an abelian category with enough
injectives. Fixing a functorial K-injective resolution
[def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] $M_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ of every
cochain complex in $\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T)$, the assignment

$$
 \Rlim:D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))\longrightarrow D(T_{\Proet},A),
 \qquad
 M_\bullet\longmapsto\varprojlim_nI_n
$$

is a triangulated functor, and any two such choices of functorial K-injective
resolutions give isomorphic functors.

Its values are sequential derived inverse limits in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit].

(*Source note:* Stacks Project, Derived Categories, Definition (Tag
[08TC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08TC)) defines the derived-limit
property by a distinguished triangle; it does not choose functorial cones.
Theorem (Tag [079P](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/079P)) supplies
functorial K-injective resolutions in a Grothendieck abelian category.
Lemma (Tag [0BK7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BK7)) gives existence
of derived limits for inverse systems of bounded-below derived objects.
The unbounded strict-tower triangulated functor and the natural comparison
between resolution choices asserted here require the argument below.)

proof.text: Let L be the actual inverse-limit functor on strict towers. It is additive by preservation of binary products. Strict towers are Grothendieck abelian by def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, so the existing K-injective derivability structure constructs L.rightDerivedFunctor and makes its universal unit invertible on every K-injective tower complex. This is completedRlim_computation.

Use the CommShift and IsTriangulated instances of the existing unbounded right-derived functor of the additive functor L. For another universal derived pair (RF, eta), Mathlib Functor.rightDerivedUnique gives a natural isomorphism from completedRlim to RF. This is completedRlim_properties and proves resolution independence through the universal derived pairs.

Exact countable products of pro-etale module sheaves give CountableAB4Star, and the derived-product theorem supplies countable products in their derived category. The ringed-site Grothendieck theorem supplies enough injectives. Represent the given derived strict tower M by a K-injective tower J using the equivalence K(Inj) with D(Tow). Construct the cone whose vertex is L applied termwise to J and whose legs are the actual limit projections; it is limiting by checking each cochain degree. Apply the canonical localized evaluation-tower Roos theorem to this cone.

The invertible right-derived unit and the chosen representation identify Q(lim J) with completedRlim(M). Exact evaluation comparison isomorphisms identify Q(J_n) with the prescribed derived evaluations of M. The defining equation of rightDerivedNatTrans, composed with rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory_hom_fac, identifies every projection under the first comparison (the private completedRlimProjection_unit lemma). Naturality of the localization lift gives the transition comparison. Product projections show that these identifications intertwine both the specified first arrow completedRlimRoosProjection and the transition endomorphism. Transport the canonical distinguished Roos triangle along the three isomorphisms; its final arrow is the original final arrow precomposed with the inverse product comparison and postcomposed with the shifted first-object comparison.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T)$ be the tower category of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], an abelian category with enough
injectives. Fixing a functorial K-injective resolution
[def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] $M_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ of every
object of $\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T)$, the assignment

$$
 \Rlim:D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))\longrightarrow D(T_{\Proet},A),
 \qquad
 M_\bullet\longmapsto\varprojlim_nI_n
$$

is a triangulated functor, and any two such choices of functorial K-injective
resolutions give isomorphic functors.

proof.text:
In a Grothendieck abelian category every complex admits a functorial
K-injective resolution, and quasi-isomorphic K-injective complexes are
chain-homotopy equivalent (Stacks Project, Theorem 19.12.6, Tag
[079P](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/079P)); applied to the tower
category of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] this supplies the
functorial resolutions fixed in the statement. By
[prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit-computation] the value of the assignment
at $M_\bullet$ represents the derived limit $\Rlim M_\bullet$ of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit], and the derived limit is a triangulated
functor of the system, being the first term of the Roos triangle, which is
natural in the system; the assignment therefore inherits exactness on
distinguished triangles. A second choice of functorial K-injective
resolutions is related to the first by a chain-homotopy equivalence over each
object, and $\varprojlim_n(-)$ of a levelwise homotopy equivalence of towers
is a homotopy equivalence, so the two assignments agree up to a natural
isomorphism of functors. The K-injectivity used here is that of
[def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions].
